archetype.name: Fringe Contender (shootout offense)
archetype.definition: A top-ten offense with a protected quarterback, tied to a pass defense at the bottom of the league, so Dallas wins when it outscores people and loses when it gives the ball away.

report.headline: Elite-adjacent offense, last-place pass defense: 2025's team again, with a softer schedule.
report.take:
Dallas is a very specific team, and history says it isn't a fluke. The offense ranks 6th in EPA per play, 4th in the play-by-play cut, and Dak Prescott has started every game behind a line that has allowed the fewest sacks in the league. The defense is last in EPA allowed and last against the pass, and opponents convert 54.7% of third downs, also last. This is almost exactly the 2025 profile: 5th in offensive EPA, 32nd in defensive EPA allowed, 30.1 points allowed a game. Seven games in, nothing suggests the defensive fix arrived.

The record understates the team slightly. Dallas has outscored opponents 189-180, and the differential implies 4.4 wins against the three it has. The gap comes from close games (a 25% one-score win rate) and from turnovers. The two worst offensive games of the year, a 24-16 home loss to Tampa Bay with three giveaways and a 23-13 loss at Green Bay with two, are the only games where the passing attack went negative in EPA. When Prescott protects the ball this offense puts up 31 to 38 points.

The box score hides two things. First, the run game looks worse than it is. Yards per carry (3.33) and stuff rate rank in the bottom six, but run success rate ranks 7th and run EPA 9th. Javonte Williams is grinding out efficient short gains, not getting blown up, and the 204-yard night in Philadelphia showed what happens against a soft front. Second, the defense isn't losing deep. Deep-pass EPA allowed sits mid-pack, while short-pass EPA allowed ranks 31st. Offenses are moving the chains underneath on a unit that barely hits the quarterback and has three takeaways. That kind of slow bleed doesn't regress away on its own.

The path forward is favorable because of the calendar. Five of the remaining ten opponents (Arizona, Indianapolis, Tennessee, Philadelphia, Washington) have losing records and offenses ranked 18th or worse, and the Giants at 4-2-1 are the only team ahead in the division. A defense this bad caps the ceiling. Against San Francisco, Jacksonville or the Rams it will need shootout wins. But this is a team that should finish with a winning record if it simply stops donating possessions.

strengths.title: Prescott's passing game drives everything
strengths.body: The offense ranks among the league's best per play, and the passing game carries it. CeeDee Lamb draws the bulk of the targets with George Pickens a strong second option. The efficiency held up across most of the schedule and matches the 2025 offense, so it looks structural rather than hot.

strengths.title: Best pass protection in football
strengths.body: Seven sacks allowed and a league-best sack rate, despite a pressure rate that only ranks 25th. Prescott is beating pressure by getting the ball out and avoiding the drive-killing negative play. Because it relies partly on the quarterback's processing, it should hold as long as he stays upright.

strengths.title: Run game more efficient than it looks
strengths.body: Yards per carry are poor, but the run game stays on schedule. Success rate and run EPA both rank in the top ten, which keeps the play-action and third-and-short game alive. Philadelphia showed the upside when the front gets movement; against good run defenses, expect grind rather than chunks.

concerns.title: Pass defense bleeds underneath and on third down
concerns.body: Dallas is last in pass EPA allowed and last on third down, and the damage is happening on short throws rather than deep shots. This is the same unit that finished 32nd in 2025, so it's a real flaw, not a slow start. It's the main reason a top-ten offense owns a losing record.

concerns.title: No pass rush, no takeaways
concerns.body: The pressure rate is respectable, but the defense rarely finishes: QB hit rate and sack rate both sit in the bottom six, and the takeaway count is among the league's lowest. With no disruption, a bad coverage unit can't steal possessions back. The linebacker room is also thin with Dee Winters and Marist Liufau out.

concerns.title: Giveaways decide its losses
concerns.body: The turnover margin is negative, which carries over from a 2025 team that ranked 30th in turnover differential. The Tampa Bay and Green Bay losses came with three and two giveaways, against a defense that can't make up for them. Some of that is noise, but the pattern is two seasons old.

trend.note: Dallas opened alternating losses and high-scoring wins, then slid with turnover-heavy losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay. It answered with its most complete game, 38-21 at Philadelphia with over 200 rushing yards and no giveaways.

nextGame.headline: Dallas's passing game meets one of the league's leakiest secondaries
nextGame.body:
Arizona comes to Dallas at 2-5 with the league's worst scoring defense, and its weakness lines up with Dallas's strength. The Cardinals rank near the bottom in pass EPA allowed, explosive pass rate allowed and deep-pass EPA, and opposing WR1s and WR2s have feasted. Where Arizona is sound is against the run and in tackling. Its offense under Jacoby Brissett is below average and leans on a slow, clock-eating approach, which matters against a Dallas defense that can't get off the field on third down. The Book has Dallas -6.5 with a 54.5 total, pricing in points on both sides.

On availability, Arizona's secondary is the story. Cornerback Max Melton and safety Andrew Wingard, both regulars, were out last week, as were defensive tackle Walter Nolen III and guard Jon Gaines II. Their return estimates point to this game, but those are estimates. Running back Jeremiyah Love was set to practice Wednesday, while James Conner remains on IR, Jalen Brooks is done for the year, and tight end Tip Reiman may not play again this season. For Dallas, linebacker Dee Winters (calf), safety P.J. Locke (foot) and linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) all sat against Philadelphia. A thinner second level is a real worry against an offense that wants to run and throw underneath.

waysToWin.title: Lamb and Pickens attack the secondary
waysToWin.body: Arizona's pass defense is among the worst in the league per play and gives up explosives at a near-league-worst rate. Opposing top two receivers have been especially productive. If Melton and Wingard sit again, this is the cleanest matchup Dallas has had all year.

waysToWin.title: Build a lead Arizona can't chase
waysToWin.body: Arizona's offense scores near the bottom of the league and its passing game ranks in the 20s. The Cardinals are built to shorten games, not win shootouts. An early two-score lead takes the clock-control plan away and forces Brissett into the kind of game Arizona has lost all season.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yardage
waysToWin.body: Arizona's special teams have cost it a real chunk of EPA per game, while Dallas's are slightly positive. In a game where the defense may struggle to get stops, field position and a short field or two can be the margin.

waysToLose.title: Arizona keeps the ball and the chains
waysToLose.body: Arizona holds the ball among the league's longest, and Dallas's defense is last on third down. Long drives of short completions would cap Dallas's possessions, shrinking the advantage its offense should hold. The missing linebackers make the underneath game harder to stop.

waysToLose.title: Another multi-giveaway afternoon
waysToLose.body: The Tampa Bay loss came as a big favorite with three turnovers despite 316 passing yards. Dallas's defense has almost no ability to win back possessions. Hand Arizona a short field twice and a 6.5-point favorite becomes a coin flip.

waysToLose.title: Run game stalls into Arizona's front
waysToLose.body: Arizona defends the run well and tackles cleanly, and Dallas already gets stuffed at a bottom-four rate. If Williams can't stay on schedule, Dallas becomes pass-only on long downs and invites the drive-killers it has mostly avoided.

nextGame.watch: Arizona's third-down conversions on long, clock-eating drives: if the Cardinals sustain them, Dallas's offense won't get enough possessions to cover.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the sustainable part. The efficiency matches 2025, the protection is elite, and Prescott has been the only starter. The defense is also sustainable, unfortunately, as a bottom-tier unit two seasons running. Expect plenty of 30-27 games. What should regress in Dallas's favor is the close-game luck and some of the turnover margin, since the point differential already says this is a .500-plus team.

The schedule does the rest. Arizona, Indianapolis, Tennessee, Philadelphia and Washington are all games Dallas should be favored in. San Francisco, Seattle's defense, the Rams and Jacksonville's offense are the tests. The NFC East is weak enough that the late home game against the Giants could decide the division. A finish around 9-8 is the middle case, with the playoff line depending on whether the defense can win even one of the hard games.
swingFactors: Whether the pass defense improves on third down
Results against SF, SEA, LA and JAX

confidence.note: Seven games is a small sample, but the profile mirrors 2025 almost exactly.
